subject: Request: EU-only processing binding commitment + VPC topology & SIG evidence
messages:
From: Clara Diaz <clara.diaz@meditrack.uk>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: Legal Ops <legal@meditrack.uk>
Date: 2026-10-05T09:14:00+01:00
Subject: EU-only processing: binding commitment + topology / evidence request

Hi Markus,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As part of our procurement/infosec review we need two things to move to final approval: a contractual binding commitment that customer data will be processed and stored only in the EU for production workloads (with explicit description of any limited exceptions), and a compact evidence bundle covering CAIQ / SIG answers and a SOC 2 snapshot focused on data residency controls.

Specific asks:
- Short binding statement we can insert into our DPA (one paragraph) that commits to EU-only processing for Customer Production data and lists permitted, documented exceptions (e.g., transient cache failover to secondary region) and how notice/controls work.
- A high-level VPC topology diagram showing how private connectivity is established (VPC peering / PrivateLink / customer-managed VPN) and where customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) can be integrated.
- SIG/CAIQ spreadsheet with controls called out for regional isolation, key management, and logging/retention.
- A SOC 2 snapshot or summary page identifying the controls we can rely on for logical separation and change management.

Timeline: Meditrack needs this for the security board on 2026-10-12. Can you confirm whether Redwood can provide a single-paragraph commitment and the attachments above by 2026-10-08? If there are any commercial implications (SLA or dedicated capacity requirements) please flag them.

Thanks,
Clara
Clara Diaz
Head of Legal & Compliance
MediTrack UK

Subject: Re: EU-only processing: binding commitment + topology / evidence request

Hi Clara — thank you, and great to see the board timeline.

Short answer: yes, we can provide a one-paragraph contractual commitment for EU-only processing for production workloads and an evidence bundle (CAIQ/SIG summary + SOC2 excerpt and topology). I want to surface two practical points up front so your legal team has context:

1) Deployment modes: we support Hosted, Dedicated (reserved GPU pool), and Private (VPC/on-prem). The exact language and operational guarantees differ by mode. EU-only binding commitments for Hosted customers are implemented via regional routing and contractual DPA language; for strict residency customers we recommend Dedicated or Private for strongest guarantees.

2) Failover carve-outs: we can include a limited, documented exception for transient failover to a non-EU region (example: Ohio) only in emergency conditions (regional outage) with:
   - documented runbook,
   - maximum timebound (e.g., 72 hours), and
   - prior notice to the customer within a defined window post-incident (or immediate notice if not possible).

I’ve looped in Neha (Legal) and Lauren (Solutions) to prepare the paragraph and the topology + SIG/CAIQ extracts. We can deliver a draft paragraph and the evidence package by EOD 2026-10-08. If Meditrack requires elimination of the failover exception entirely, we will note impacts on resilience and may recommend Dedicated/Private plus additional contractual terms (and an ops runbook).

Action items assigned:
- Neha: draft DPA paragraph and identify any non-standard contractual language.
- Lauren: produce VPC topology diagram and SIG/CAIQ mapping.
- Markus (me): coordinate SOC2 extract and confirm whether Hosted plan suffices or Dedicated/Private is recommended.

Markus
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference

Hi all — I drafted a compact paragraph you can drop into the DPA. I put it in plain language for procurement and then added an annotated clause for legal review.

DPA paragraph (procurement-friendly):
"Redwood Inference will process and store Customer Production Data solely within the European Union for the duration of the Agreement. In the event of a documented regional service disruption affecting EU infrastructure, Redwood may (as a last resort) route transient processing to an alternative data center for the shortest necessary period to restore service, subject to the emergency runbook and notification procedures set out in Schedule X. Redwood will not use such failover for operational cost optimization or routine load balancing."

Annotated legal note (for counsel):
- Define "Customer Production Data" with reference to the data classification annex.
- Limit failover to specific infrastructure events and cap maximum residence time (we propose 72 hours) and require post-incident report including logs and locations.
- For customers requiring absolute EU-only residency without any exceptions, Redwood offers Dedicated or Private deployment options; we'll include optional schedule language to tie residency guarantees to specific deployment types and associated SLA credits.

I also attached a short checklist of legal evidence items we can supply:
- SIG/CAIQ export (redwood answers, highlight EU isolation controls)
- SOC 2 report excerpt (controls mapping)
- KMS/HSM integration guide excerpt
- Ops runbook excerpt for failover and notification

I'll attach the DPA paragraph as a text stub and mark-up options for your team to redline.

Neha Kapoor
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: EU-only processing: binding commitment + topology / evidence request

Hi Clara — attaching the topology diagram and the SIG/CAIQ mapping you requested. Below are the practical implementation notes and a short ops runbook excerpt so your engineering team can validate compatibility.

Quick answers:
- VPC connectivity options: PrivateLink (recommended), customer-managed VPN, or dedicated interconnect. PrivateLink + customer-side peering keeps all control-plane traffic landing inside your VPC while model inference runs on Redwood-managed hosts in the selected EU region.
- KMS/HSM: we support customer-managed keys via KMS integration (bring-your-own-key). Keys remain under customer control and are not exported.
- Logging and retention: request-level logs and tokenization events are logged in the customer's audit stream and retained per DPA; we can provide log-export connectors to your SIEM (S3 or GCS buckets in EU region).

Ops runbook excerpt (failover):
1) Trigger: EU region P95 request error rate > 50% sustained for 15 minutes AND region-level provider outage declared.
2) Approval: on-call infra lead + CS lead must approve emergency failover.
3) Action: failover routing enabled to pre-configured secondary region (only if Dedicated or Hosted customers with elected failover option).
4) Limit: 72 hours automatic cap; any extension requires written authorization from customer legal/ops.
5) Notification: immediate incident post to designated contacts and follow-up report within 48 hours with logs and KV cache snapshot.

Attached: 
- redwood-eu-vpc-topology.png (high-level diagram)
- eu-only-processing-ops-runbook.pdf (excerpt)
- SIG-response-summary.csv (control-by-control mapping)

If Meditrack wants a zero-exception residency guarantee, we recommend Dedicated or Private and will provide updated SLA and deployment checklist. Happy to hop on a short call with your infra/security folks — suggest 30 minutes early next week.

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
